He played college basketball for the [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State Wolfpack]] and spent several seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Born in the United States, he plays for the [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spanish national team]] and helped lead them to a [[EuroBasket]] title in [[EuroBasket 2022|2022]]. ==High school career== Brown initially attended [[Centennial High School (Roswell, Georgia)|Centennial High School]] in his native [[Roswell, Georgia]] ([[United States]]). He averaged 20.8 points as a senior and was named a fourth-team Parade All-American and the Georgia 5A player of the Year. When he graduated in 2009, he was the No. 36 nationally and the No. 7 shooting guard overall by Rivals.com. After he graduated, he attended the [[Hargrave Military Academy]] in [[Chatham, Virginia]].{{cite web |url=http://www.gopack.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=624 |title=North Carolina State bio |work=GoPack.com |access-date=January 29, 2016}} ==College career== [[File:Lorenzo Brown.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Brown at NC State.]] Brown, a 6'5" [[Guard (basketball)|guard]], played for [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] from 2010 to 2013. He started all three seasons and led the Wolfpack to consecutive [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]] appearances in [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012]] and [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2013]]. As a junior, Brown averaged 12.4 [[Points per game|points]] and 4.3 [[rebounds per game]] and led the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) in [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] with 7.2 per game.{{cite web |title=Lorenzo Brown Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/lorenzo-brown-1.html |access-date=September 26, 2013}} At the close of the season, Brown was named second team All-ACC.{{cite web |title=Howell One of Four Pack Players To Earn All-ACC Accolades |work=GoPack.com |date=March 11, 2013 |url=http://www.gopack.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031113aaj.html |access-date=September 26, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928223053/http://www.gopack.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031113aaj.html |archive-date=September 28, 2013}} During his college career Brown averaged 11.6 points, 4.2 rebounds, 5.8 assists and 32.6 minutes per game. After the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 season]], Brown decided to forgo his final season of college eligibility and declared for the [[2013 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=North Carolina State's Lorenzo Brown declares for NBA draft |work=SI.com |date=March 27, 2013 |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/college-basketball/news/20130327/lorenzo-brown-nc-state-nba-draft.ap/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130929220610/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/college-basketball/news/20130327/lorenzo-brown-nc-state-nba-draft.ap/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=29 September 2013 |access-date=September 26, 2013}} ==Professional career== ===2013–14 season=== Brown was selected with the 52nd overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the Minnesota Timberwolves{{cite news |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1671599-lorenzo-brown-picked-by-minnesota-timberwolves-scouting-report-and-analysis |title=Lorenzo Brown Picked by Minnesota Timberwolves: Scouting Report and Analysis |first=Jonathan |last=Wasserman |date=June 27, 2013 |work=BleacherReport.com |access-date=December 21, 2013}} and subsequently joined the team for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On September 26, 2013, he signed his first professional contract with the Timberwolves.{{cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-brown-hummel-and-jeffers-camp-roster |title=Wolves Sign Brown, Hummel And Jeffers To Camp Roster |date=September 26, 2013 |work=NBA.com |access-date=December 21, 2013}} However, he was waived by Timberwolves on October 25, 2013.{{cite provide backcourt depth to Drive |work=mlive.com |date=March 3, 2017 |access-date=March 4, 2017}} ===2017–18 season=== Brown joined the [[Detroit Pistons]] for the 2017 [[NBA Summer League]]. He ultimately signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Toronto Raptors]]. Under the terms of the deal, split time between the Raptors and their G League affiliate, the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite news |title=Raptors Sign Lorenzo Brown |url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sign-lorenzo-brown |access-date=July 25, 2017 |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 25, 2017}} He also became the first player who previously had NBA experience to sign a two-way contract with an NBA team. He won the [[NBA G League Most Valuable Player Award]] for the season with Raptors 905.{{cite web |url=http://gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905s-lorenzo-brown-named-2017-2018-nba-g-league-valuable-player/ |title=Raptors 905's Lorenzo Brown Named 2017–2018 NBA G League Most Valuable Player |publisher=[[NBA G League]] |date=April 10, 2018}} Prior to the close of the season, Brown's contract was upgraded to a standard deal.{{cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-lorenzo-brown-upgraded-to-regular-contract/ |title=Raptors' Lorenzo Brown: Upgraded to regular contract |publisher=[[CBSSports.com]] |date=April 11, 2018}} ===2018–19 season=== On July 20, 2018, the Raptors re-signed Brown.{{cite web |title=Raptors sign guard Lorenzo Brown, Canadian forward Chris Boucher |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/raptors-agree-training-camp-deal-canadian-chris-boucher/ |website=Sportsnet |access-date=July 20, 2018}} In 26 games for the team during the [[2018-19 NBA season|2018–19 season]], Brown averaged 2.1 points per game in 8.2 minutes per game. On January 7, 2019, the Raptors waived Brown.{{cite web |title=Raptors Waive Lorenzo Brown |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-waive-lorenzo-brown |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 7, 2019}} On February 10, 2019, [[Guangzhou Loong Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] was reported to have signed Brown.{{cite news |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano |title=Lorenzo Brown signs with Guangzhou |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/lorenzo-brown-signs-with-guangzhou |date=February 10, 2019 |newspaper=Sportando |access-date=February 10, 2019}}{{cite web |title=广州队新签1米96外援 将使用双小外组合 |url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/basketball/cba/2019-02-11/doc-ihrfqzka4825639.shtml |date=February 10, 2019 |website=sina.com.cn |language=zh |access-date=February 10, 2019}} Brown made his debut for the Loong Lions two days later, scoring 17 points with 2 rebounds and a steal in a 97–93 victory over the [[Beijing Ducks]].{{cite web |title=Regular Season Round 40: Beijing Ducks – Guangzhou LL 93–97 |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2019/0212_941_3514.asp |date=February 12, 2019 |website=eurobasket.com |access-date=February 12, 2019}} In eight games he averaged 25.2 points, 5.4 rebounds, 4.9 assists, and 2.8 steals per game, and shot 80% from the free throw line. ===Crvena zvezda=== On August 3, 2019, [[KK Crvena zvezda]] announced that they had signed Brown.{{cite web |title=Lorenco Braun pojačao crveno-beli zid!!! |language=sr |url=http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/lorenco-braun-pojacao-crveno-beli-zid-03-08-2019.html |date=August 3, 2019 |website=kkcrvenazvezda.rs |access-date=August 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190803092627/http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/lorenco-braun-pojacao-crveno-beli-zid-03-08-2019.html |archive-date=August 3, 2019 |url-status=dead}}{{cite web |title=Lorenzo Brown reinforced the red and white squad |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=42140 |date=August 3, 2019 |website=aba-liga.com |access-date=August 3, 2019}} He averaged 11.3 points, 2.9 rebounds, 5.1 assists, and 1.2 steals per game, and shot 84% from the free throw line. ===Fenerbahçe=== On July 14, 2020, he signed with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe Beko]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Basketball Super League]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/635759/Fenerbahce-signs-Lorenzo-Brown,-ex-Crvena-Zvezda |title=Fenerbahce signs Lorenzo Brown, ex Crvena Zvezda |date=July 14, 2020 |publisher=Eurobasket |language=En |access-date=July 14, 2020}} He averaged 10.3 points, 2.4 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 1.3 steals per game, and shot 83% from the free throw line. On June 17, 2021, Brown was released from the Turkish club. ===UNICS Kazan=== On July 23, 2021, Brown signed a one-year contract with [[BC UNICS|UNICS]].{{cite news |title=Unics Kazan announces Lorenzo Brown |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/unics-kazan-announces-lorenzo-brown/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 23, 2021 |date=July 23, 2021 |last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro}} He left the team in early 2022 due to the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], but returned later to finish the season.{{Cite web |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1316372/unics-kazan-reportedly-suing-jarrel-brantley-for-250000/ |title=Unics Kazan reportedly suing Jarrell Brantley for $250,000 |date=March 4, 2022 |website=Eurohoops}}{{Cite web |url=https://newswep.com/more-than-50-people-which-of-the-foreigners-left-the-russian-sports-clubs-football-rbc-sport/ |title=More than 50 people. Which of the foreigners left the Russian sports clubs: RBC Sport |date=March 5, 2022}} He averaged 13.7 points, 3.6 rebounds, 5.6 assists, and 1.3 steals per game, and shot 85% from the free throw line. ===Maccabi Tel Aviv=== On June 29, 2022, Brown signed a two-year deal with Israeli club [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].{{Cite web |url=https://basketnews.com/news-174300-lorenzo-brown-officially-signs-a-two-year-deal-with-maccabi-tel-aviv.html |title=Lorenzo Brown officially signs a two-year deal with Maccabi Tel Aviv |date=June 29, 2022 |website=BasketNews}} In 2022–23, he averaged 16.4 points, 2.7 rebounds, 5.7 assists, and 1.0 steals per game, and shot 89% from the free throw line. In February, Brown signed a contract extension with Maccabi until the end of the 2025–26 season.{{Cite web |url=https://basketnews.com/news-185024-lorenzo-brown-extends-his-contract-with-maccabi-tel-aviv.html |title=Lorenzo Brown extends his contract with Maccabi Tel Aviv |date=February 9, 2023 |website=BasketNews}} ===Panathinaikos=== On June 19, 2024, Brown agreed upon a three-year contract, worth €5.4 million (along with a €600,000 buyout compensation for [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi]]), with the reigning [[EuroLeague]] champions [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]]. The deal was made official on June 25, 2024. Despite the length of the contract, Brown left the club in 2025 following an underwhelming season in which his performances did not meet expectations. As part of the agreement to terminate the contract early, Panathinaikos paid him a compensation of €700,000 to facilitate the move.{{Cite web |title=Lorenzo Brown leaves Panathinaikos for Milano |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1876543/lorenzo-brown-departs-panathinaikos-signs-with-milano/ |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=Eurohoops}} ===Olimpia Milano=== On July 12, 2025, Brown signed a multi-year contract with Italian powerhouse [[Olimpia Milano]].{{Cite web |title=Lorenzo Brown signs with Olimpia Milano |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1876545/lorenzo-brown-officially-joins-olimpia-milano/ |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=Eurohoops}} In October 2025, Brown missed the opening two games of the Euroleague season due to a left thigh strain.{{Cite web |date=2025-10-16 |title=Lorenzo Brown suffers left calf injury |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1881395/lorenzo-brown-suffers-left-calf-injury/ |access-date=2025-10-16 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}} ==National team career== After being a [[naturalization]] target for Croatia,{{cite news |last=Radičević |first=Vlado |url=https://www.tportal.hr/sport/clanak/kad-nece-hrvati-hoce-spanjolci-a-ima-ih-47-milijuna-amerikancu-kojeg-obozava-hezonja-hitno-su-dali-drzavljanstvo-a-zna-se-i-razlog-20220705 |title=Kad neće Hrvati, hoće Španjolci, a ima ih 47 milijuna! Amerikancu kojeg obožava Hezonja hitno su dali državljanstvo, a zna se i razlog |agency=TPortal.hr |date=5 July 2022 |access-date=14 February 2023}}{{cite news |author1=[[Jordan Taylor (basketball)|Jordan Taylor]] |author2=Anthony Goods |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dusvOOOjOVM&t=1769s |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/dusvOOOjOVM |archive-date=14 February 2023 |url-status=live |title=Episode 30: Lorenzo Brown Talks NBA 10 day Contracts, Eurobasket, Spanish Nationality, EuroLeague & More (timestamp 29:29) |agency=Role Player podcast |date=30 January 2023 |access-date=14 February 2023}}{{cite news |url=https://basketnews.com/news-178223-lorenzo-brown-was-offered-to-croatia.html |title=Lorenzo Brown was offered to Croatia |agency=BasketNews.com |date=20 September 2022 |access-date=14 February 2023}} Brown was granted [[Spanish citizenship]] in early July 2022 ahead of [[EuroBasket 2022]].{{Cite web |date=2022-07-05 |title=Lorenzo Brown was granted Spanish citizenship |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurobasket/1365336/lorenzo-brown-to-play-for-spain-national-team-eurobasket/ |access-date=2022-07-05 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}}{{cite news |last=Tsakos |first=Alexandros |url=https://hedgeout.net/2022/07/05/lorenzo-brown-acquires-spanish-nationality/ |title=Lorenzo Brown acquires Spanish nationality |agency=HedgeOut.com |date=5 July 2022 |access-date=14 February 2023}}{{cite news |last=Harpidis |first=Christos |url=https://twitter.com/chrisalucard/status/1544210638330859524 |title=Lorenzo Brown obtains Spanish nationality and will be able to play the FIBA Eurobasket 22 with Spain |agency=Christos Harpidis Twitter feed |date=5 July 2022 |access-date=14 February 2023}} Brown stated that the prospect of being coached at the Spain national team by [[Sergio Scariolo]]—whom he had previously collaborated with at the [[Toronto Raptors]]—was the deciding factor the player chose Spain. He represented [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain]] at [[EuroBasket 2022]], winning gold in the final against [[France men's national basketball team|France]].
